slot.brief: A mirror forms an image with given object distance and magnification (or find image position); apply the mirror formula with sign conventions.

stem: An object is placed $20$ cm in front of a spherical mirror. Its image is virtual and upright, with magnification $+2$. Using the Cartesian sign convention, the focal length of the mirror is
working:
$u=-20$ cm, $m=-\dfrac{v}{u}=+2\Rightarrow v=+40$ cm
$\dfrac{1}{f}=\dfrac{1}{v}+\dfrac{1}{u}=\dfrac{1}{40}-\dfrac{1}{20}=-\dfrac{1}{40}$
$f=-40$ cm

Independent check: With u = -20 cm and m = -v/u = +2, v = +40 cm. Then 1/f = 1/v + 1/u = 1/40 - 1/20 = -1/40, so f = -40 cm.
solution:
Using $m=-v/u$ and $u=-20\text{ cm}$,
$$+2=-\frac{v}{-20}\implies v=+40\text{ cm}.$$
The mirror formula gives $\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{40}-\frac{1}{20}=-\frac{1}{40}$, hence $f=-40\text{ cm}$.
